Package dev.opencollab.paletter

Class Paletter

java.lang.Object
dev.opencollab.paletter.Paletter
public final class Paletter extends Object
Entry point: vanilla Bedrock data for every supported version, and the palettes compiled from it. 

 Paletter paletter = Paletter.bundled();
 PaletteLayer layer = PaletteLayer.builder("server")...build();

 // Once per client version, shared by all sessions on it
 Palette palette = paletter.palette(codec);
 // Optionally per session, sharing everything it does not change
 Palette sessionPalette = palette.extend(sessionLayer);
Everything is loaded lazily and cached; instances are thread safe. Block states and item components that are equal across versions are the same instances. Share one instance for the whole application: every per-version palette it compiles is cached in it.

Null handling: parameters and return values are @NonNull unless the signature says @Nullable; passing null where it is not allowed is a bug and throws NullPointerException. A lookup that finds nothing returns null (version(String)).

Errors: methods throw only for configuration errors, which are reported by IllegalArgumentException (a version that does not exist) or PaletteException (content that cannot be compiled). Problems with data the library compiles that do not stop it are entries of the PaletteReport instead. A data source that cannot load its files throws UncheckedIOException.

Concepts: a Palette is the compiled content of one client version. Content is named by keys (version independent identities, such as BedrockBlockType); a palette hands out definitions (what is sent) and resolutions (what it makes of a key). See Palette.

Canonical ids (canonicalBlocks(), canonicalItems()) are defined by the newest version, and valid in every palette of this instance.

Since:
1.0.0

    • verifiedBuilds

      public @NonNull List<VerifiedBuild> verifiedBuilds(@NonNull DataVersion version)
      The Bedrock Dedicated Server release builds that were run and found to send a data version's data: the build it was captured from and the builds compared with it and found identical, oldest first. The list may hold the capture build alone. A data version serves every protocol from its first one up to the next version's; a build or protocol that is not in this list is served the same data, unverified.
      Parameters:
      version - a data version of this instance's data source
      Returns:
      the builds, oldest first; empty when the data source records none (a preview, or data of another source)
      Since:
      1.0.0
      See Also:
      • PaletteDataSource.verifiedBuilds(DataVersion)

    • palette

      public @NonNull Palette palette(int protocolVersion)
      The palette of a protocol version: vanilla content plus this instance's layers, compiled once per data version and cached. Session content goes on top of it with Palette.extend(PaletteLayer). A protocol newer than all data gets the newest data, with an info entry in the report; content the client has that the data lacks is then missing.
      Parameters:
      protocolVersion - a Bedrock protocol version number
      Returns:
      the palette serving it, never null
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the protocol version is older than all data
      PaletteException - if a layer of this instance cannot be compiled
      Since:
      1.0.0
